reviewed_by: human visual review (cv2 contact-sheet frame extraction) cross-checked against the raw MediaPipe knee/hip angle trace from scripts/evaluate_squat.py --trace
method: Each clip was first resampled into labeled contact-sheet images (cv2, ~0.13-0.4s spacing, finer 0.06-0.2s spacing around ambiguous transitions) and inspected before running any evaluator. Where the visual read and the angle trace disagreed, the angle trace was treated as authoritative for DEPTH/EXTENSION (a silhouette's torso lean is a poor proxy for knee angle; see the methodology note below) while the visual review stayed authoritative for things eyeballing is actually reliable for: presence/absence of a rep attempt, camera angle, occlusion, full-body framing, and start/end standing timing.
methodology_note: Initial thumbnail-only review of squat_side_01.mp4 misjudged 5 real reps as '1 clear rep plus 7.5s of non-standard movement' because the subject's torso stayed pitched forward the whole time and the reviewer was reading torso angle, not knee angle. The raw knee-angle trace (docs/verification/2026-09-21/baseline/traces/squat_side_01.csv) shows the knee cycling cleanly between ~55-100 degrees (bottom) and ~150-178 degrees (near-full extension) on a steady ~1.8s rhythm -- genuine repeated squats, just with unusually heavy forward trunk lean. Ground truth below reflects the corrected, angle-verified counts. Do not repeat the mistake of eyeballing depth from torso posture alone in future verification passes.

final_holdout_status: INCOMPLETE. Only squat_negative_01.mp4 qualifies as an independent final-holdout clip after this pass -- it was never used to diagnose the counting fix and its expected result (0 reps) is unaffected by it. squat_normal_01.mp4 and squat_normal_02.mp4 both meet the depth/count bar but were the exact clips used to find and justify the standing-confirm-timing fix in squat_counter.py, so counting them as final proof would be validation leakage; they are DEV clips now. squat_shallow_01.mp4 fails the shooting protocol (no 2s pre-roll stand hides 3 of 5 attempts from the app) and has inconsistent depth, so it cannot serve as a clean shallow-rejection holdout either. squat_front_01.mp4 and squat_side_01.mp4 are off-protocol camera angles (0 deg and ~90 deg instead of ~45 deg). Net: do not report 100% final-holdout accuracy from this data set. See the verification report's 'what to shoot next' section for the specific new clips needed (a normal-depth 45-degree clip not used in this debugging session, and a shallow clip with a genuine 2s pre-roll stand and consistently sub-threshold depth).
